answer: Copying the same citations across 267 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 267 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the sable index resolves every citation against the ferrous checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the kernel audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 4938 identities would post 4089 proofs and burn roughly 62 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
